# stage: plan

You consume `ticket`. You must produce `approach`, `evidence-plan`.

The orchestrator owns this stage's rows: read consumes with
`run_field_get`, write produces with `run_field_set {stage: "plan"}`, and
end a failure with `run_stage {action: fail, stage: "plan", reason}`.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
%% name: plan
    plan_entered([Plan stage entered])
    run_field_get_ticket[/"run_field_get {key: ticket}"/]
    read_ticket
    next_move_after_ticket{Next move after reading the ticket?}
    stop_code_before_triage[STOP: no code, no file, no implementer dispatch before the printed block]:::stop
    pick_tier
    print_triage_block
    gate_plan
    plan_answer{plan answer?}
    run_decision_strategy[/"run_decision {contract: execution-strategy@1, scope: run, selection: {tier}, decidedBy: stage-plan}"/]
    run_field_set_approach[/"run_field_set {key: approach, value: <the recorded tier>, stage: plan}"/]
    run_field_set_evidence_plan[/"run_field_set {key: evidence-plan, value: <the EVIDENCE value>, stage: plan}"/]
    hand_back_go_back(((Hand the Go back answer to the orchestrator)))
    run_hold[/"run_hold {runDb, stage: plan, reason, decidedBy}"/]
    held_end_turn(((Held: end the turn naming run and stage)))
    plan_done(((Plan done: return to the orchestrator))):::done
    plan_entered --> run_field_get_ticket
    run_field_get_ticket --> read_ticket
    read_ticket --> next_move_after_ticket
    next_move_after_ticket -->|triage: pick the tier| pick_tier
    next_move_after_ticket -->|tempted to start on the code| stop_code_before_triage
    stop_code_before_triage --> pick_tier
    pick_tier --> print_triage_block
    print_triage_block --> gate_plan
    gate_plan --> plan_answer
    plan_answer -->|proceed| run_decision_strategy
    plan_answer -->|iterate: re-read with their note| read_ticket
    plan_answer -->|go back| hand_back_go_back
    plan_answer -->|hold| run_hold
    run_hold --> held_end_turn
    run_decision_strategy --> run_field_set_approach
    run_field_set_approach --> run_field_set_evidence_plan
    run_field_set_evidence_plan --> plan_done
```

## Pick the tier

**REQUIRED SUB-FLOW:** follow the strategy flow below to pick the tier.
The three tiers are its strategies of the same names; its other
strategies are not tiers of this stage. The domain may set a tier floor.



<!-- part: include:execution-strategy source=mattstack:execution-strategy version=0.32.23 path=attachments/execution-strategy/SKILL.md lines=8-96 -->
# Execution Strategy

Given a unit of work and the surface it will execute on, name the method
the executor runs and the report contract that method produces. A brief
that names no method leaves its executor to improvise one.

## The six strategies

| Strategy | Executor runs |
|---|---|
| `trivial` | the change directly; no test, because there is no runtime behavior to test |
| `direct-tdd` | superpowers:test-driven-development inline: RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR, failing test named before code |
| `from-spec` | the superpowers chain entered at the supplied spec: writing-plans, then subagent-driven-development |
| `from-plan` | superpowers:subagent-driven-development on the supplied plan |
| `superpowers` | the full chain: brainstorming -> spec -> writing-plans -> subagent-driven-development |
| `delegate` | triages against this table, picks one of the other five, runs it |

`delegate` never picks itself, must respect the surface table below, and
names its choice in its report so the dispatcher knows which report
contract applies.

Excluded: superpowers:executing-plans -- it defers to
subagent-driven-development wherever subagents are available, and
dispatched workers are full Claude Code sessions, so it is dominated.

## Picking the strategy

- `trivial` -- no runtime behavior to test: pure docs, comments, config,
  or a mechanical rename with zero logic change.
- `direct-tdd` -- real code with clear criteria and an existing pattern.
- `superpowers` -- everything else: new features, multiple valid
  approaches, vague criteria, cross-layer work, product decisions.
- `from-spec` -- a completed spec is already supplied.
- `from-plan` -- a completed plan is already supplied.
- `delegate` -- the dispatcher is not triaging; the executor triages
  against this section and picks one of the other five.

When in doubt between `direct-tdd` and `superpowers`, go `superpowers`;
between `trivial` and `direct-tdd`, go `direct-tdd`.

TDD is the floor, never a tier: any path that writes production code
writes its failing test first. `trivial` is the single escape hatch and it
is tight -- "it's simple", "it's small", or "I'll test after" is the
`direct-tdd` tell, not a `trivial` pass.

## Surface support

| Surface | `trivial` | `direct-tdd` | `from-spec` | `from-plan` | `superpowers` | `delegate` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pane worker with a question relay | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Agent-tool subagent | yes | yes | yes | yes | **no** | yes |

`superpowers` starts with brainstorming, which needs a human in the loop
throughout; an Agent-tool subagent cannot stop and wait for one.

When the picking rules land on `superpowers` and the surface is an
Agent-tool subagent, the unit fails on this surface: report the conflict
to the dispatcher rather than recording a strategy the surface cannot
run (not `superpowers`-and-continue, not a downgraded tier to fit the
surface). Name the two re-dispatch paths in the report: a pane worker
with a question relay, or a supplied spec or plan that re-enters the work
as `from-spec` or `from-plan`, which this surface supports.

## One plan, one executor

A plan is never sliced across parallel executors: it has one sequential
controller, its tasks chain by Consumes/Produces interfaces, and its
ledger is keyed by plan identity within one worktree. Fan out one level
up: 1 job = 1 sub-project = 1 spec = 1 plan = 1 branch = 1 worktree =
1 ledger.

## Report shape is per strategy

| Strategy | Report |
|---|---|
| `trivial`, `direct-tdd` | item-coded: one line per task item, plus verification results |
| `from-spec`, `superpowers` | milestone lines (`spec: <path>`, `plan: <path>`) as they land, then commit range and final-review verdict |
| `from-plan` | commit range and final-review verdict |
| `delegate` | the chosen strategy's shape, with the choice named first |

## Briefing an executor

When the caller has no brief-assembly verb, copy the assigned strategy's
body from `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../../attachments/stage-plan/parts/include-execution-strategy/references/strategies.md` verbatim into the
brief and fill its `<angle-bracket>` slots yourself. A caller that has one
(the `herd_brief` tool and its `strategy`/`strategies` fields) does this copy
for you -- name the strategy and pass it, nothing more. Either way, do not
compose method prose per job; the bodies carry the worker-boundary rules
and the report contract.

blocks.title: Print the triage block
blocks.label: Print triage block
blocks.summary: <HARD-GATE> Print the block before any implementation action: before writing or editing code, before creating a file, before dispatching an implementer…
blocks.text:
## Print the triage block

<HARD-GATE>
Print the block before any implementation action: before writing or
editing code, before creating a file, before dispatching an implementer
subagent. Not optional, not internal reasoning, not skippable for
"obvious" work.
</HARD-GATE>

Print verbatim, one tier, plus every line the domain policy defines,
exactly as it specifies:

> APPROACH: trivial -- <one-line reason>
> EVIDENCE: <per the domain policy; "none -- no policy bound" otherwise>

> APPROACH: direct-tdd -- <one-line reason>
> FAILING TEST: <the test you will write first, named>
> EVIDENCE: <as above>

> APPROACH: superpowers -- <one-line reason>
> EVIDENCE: <as above>

On direct-tdd the FAILING TEST line is mandatory: naming the test before
touching code is the point. Record nothing yet: the printed block is the
proposal, and the gate records the decision.

| Thought | Reality |
|---|---|
| "This is an obvious one-line fix, I'll just do it" | Print the block. An obvious fix is `direct-tdd`, not an exemption. |
| "I'll state the approach after I look at the code" | The gate is before code, not after. Print it now. |
| "It's basically trivial" | Only docs, config or a rename are trivial. Behavior change is direct-tdd. |
| "I already know this is a superpowers job" | Say so. The block is how the human and the run verify the triage. |
| "I'll skip the FAILING TEST line, I know what I'll test" | Then writing it costs nothing. Skipping it is how TDD becomes tests-after. |
| "The tier is obvious, I'll record it and move on" | Printing is the proposal. Recording without the gate takes the human's decision. |

## Gate plan (table below)

Walk gate-protocol's Runs integration with kind `plan`, `runDb` and
`stage: "plan"`; the gate tools record the answers. One sentence above the
form: the printed tier and why.

| Question | Options (recommended first) | Shown when |
|---|---|---|
| `tier` (write-in) | the printed tier, its label ending ` (Recommended)`, then the other two | always |
| `failing_test` | the FAILING TEST line to keep, or their rename as text | direct-tdd |
| the domain's own | as the domain policy words them | the domain declares them |
| `next` | **Proceed** / **Iterate here** / **Go back** / **Hold** | always |
| `to` | one option per earlier stage, split `to-1`, ... over 4 | Go back answered and more than one earlier stage row |

Write `approach` = the tier the gate recorded and `evidence-plan` = the
EVIDENCE value, after the `execution-strategy@1` record: the gate tools
record the gate's answers, not that contract.
Hold passes their words (or `held`) as `reason` and the gate result's
`decidedBy`.

blocks.title: Gate protocol
blocks.label: Gate protocol
blocks.summary: The daemon's gate registry is the single arbiter; under a run the gate tools record the decision.
blocks.text:
The daemon's gate registry is the single arbiter; under a run the gate
tools record the decision.

If a site's questions or a rule in the including verb ask for a move this
graph marks STOP, open the Off-script gate (below) instead.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
%% name: gate_protocol
    trigger_site_reaches([Trigger: a site reaches its gate])
    build_questions
    trigger_site_opened([Trigger: a site opened its gate with gate_open])
    gate_ask[/"gate_ask {questions, kind: <scope>, context?, subject?, runDb?, stage?}"/]
    gate_ask_result{gate_ask result?}
    ask_under_run{"Under a run (gate_ask fix)?"}
    run_budget_fix[/"run_budget {key: gate-fix:<scope>, limit: 2, stage}"/]
    fixed_ask_once{Fixed this gate_ask call once already?}
    fix_refusal
    daemon_down_unattended{Daemon down: is the gated pane unattended?}
    fail_stage_at_gate{Under a run: fail the stage at the gate?}
    run_stage_fail[/"run_stage {action: fail, stage, reason: <the gate_ask refusal, verbatim>}"/]
    present_form_no_registry
    no_registry_under_run{"Under a run (no-registry answer)?"}
    gate_record[/"gate_record {runDb, stage, scope, shape: answers, answers, decidedBy: pane}"/]
    pane_action{paneAction?}
    boards_to_open{A boards@1 context in an attended session, with a board not yet opened?}
    open_board[/open <board path>/]
    present_pane_form
    form_result{Gate form result?}
    map_answer
    gate_answer[/"gate_answer {id, answers, runDb?, stage?}"/]
    gate_answer_result{gate_answer result?}
    remap_under_run{"Under a run (answer remap)?"}
    run_budget_remap[/"run_budget {key: gate-remap:<scope>, limit: 2, stage}"/]
    resubmitted_once{Resubmitted this gate_answer once already?}
    say_surface
    hold_under_run{Holding an open gate: under a run?}
    run_field_set[/"run_field_set {key: waiting-gate, value: <id>, stage}"/]
    rt_gate_wait[/rt gate wait <id> as a background Bash task/]
    end_turn_holding
    trigger_wait_finished([Trigger: the gate wait finished])
    trigger_human_words([Trigger: the human answers in words])
    trigger_doorbell([Trigger: a doorbell push arrives])
    gate_reconcile[/"gate_reconcile {id, runDb?, stage?}"/]
    reconcile_status{gate_reconcile status?}
    write_in_to_act{"A write-in to act on (actOnWriteIn)?"}
    act_write_in
    stop_no_invented_answer[STOP: never invent an answer or re-ask a closed gate]:::stop
    stage_failed(((Gate stage failed)))
    verb_ends(((Verb ends quoting the refusal)))
    held_no_run(((No run: held at the open gate)))
    late_signal(((Late gate signal discarded)))
    path_ended(((Path ended per the verb's policy)))
    write_in_new_gate(((Write-in acted on: a new gate opens)))
    act_on_answer(((Act on the gate answer at the site))):::done
    trigger_site_reaches --> build_questions
    build_questions --> gate_ask
    gate_ask --> gate_ask_result
    gate_ask_result -->|ok| pane_action
    gate_ask_result -->|refused: daemon unreachable| daemon_down_unattended
    gate_ask_result -->|refused: other| ask_under_run
    ask_under_run -->|yes| run_budget_fix
    ask_under_run -->|no| fixed_ask_once
    run_budget_fix --> fixed_ask_once
    fixed_ask_once -->|no| fix_refusal
    fixed_ask_once -->|yes| fail_stage_at_gate
    fix_refusal --> gate_ask
    daemon_down_unattended -->|no| present_form_no_registry
    daemon_down_unattended -->|yes| fail_stage_at_gate
    fail_stage_at_gate -->|yes| run_stage_fail
    fail_stage_at_gate -->|no| verb_ends
    run_stage_fail --> stage_failed
    present_form_no_registry --> no_registry_under_run
    no_registry_under_run -->|yes| gate_record
    no_registry_under_run -->|no| write_in_to_act
    gate_record --> write_in_to_act
    trigger_site_opened --> pane_action
    pane_action -->|form| boards_to_open
    boards_to_open -->|yes: the next board| open_board
    boards_to_open -->|no, or every board opened| present_pane_form
    open_board --> boards_to_open
    pane_action -->|wait| rt_gate_wait
    present_pane_form --> form_result
    form_result -->|answered| map_answer
    form_result -.->|dismissed| trigger_doorbell
    form_result -->|cancelled| hold_under_run
    map_answer --> gate_answer
    gate_answer --> gate_answer_result
```

blocks.title: Build the gate's questions and context
blocks.label: Build questions
blocks.summary: Open before anything that depends on the answer.
blocks.text:
### Build the gate's questions and context

Open before anything that depends on the answer. A question is `{"id",
"label", "multi", "options"}`, plus `"writeIn": true` where the site marks
`(write-in)`; `kind` is the gate's scope. Pass `subject` only for a subject
not your own.

- **Context** is a VERBATIM QUOTE of the material under decision (the
  brief's task, the plan section, the failing output), never a fresh
  summary, and never sent empty. Lay it out as Markdown that reads the same
  unrendered: a framing line, then label lines (`Important:`) with one `-`
  bullet per item. Never trim it; the daemon drops what overflows. A
  question's own `context` sets up that question alone; an option's
  `description` is its one-line why.
- **Options** are `{value, label}` objects when values are not
  human-readable; a recommended pick's `label` ends ` (Recommended)`, its
  `value` bare. In a site table headed `Options (recommended first)`, mark
  the option the table writes; a row with none, such as the stage-end
  `next`, marks none.
- **`next` values** are exactly `proceed`, `iterate`, `go-back`, `hold`,
  and `abandon` or `done` where offered; the tools read `proceed` and
  `iterate`.
- **Write-ins** go only on a decision question whose free text you can act
  on, never on `next` or a review-post, respond, doctor or pane-attention
  question.
- **At most 4 options per question**, or the whole gate goes to the wait.
  Navigation (Iterate here, Go back, Hold, Abandon) is its own `next`
  question; a longer list splits into `<id>-1`, `<id>-2`, ... read as one
  union.

too.

### A boards@1 context in an attended session, with a board not yet opened?

A terminal form cannot show an image, so in an attended session (see
Attendance) a gate whose context is `boards@1` opens each board on Bash
before its form: `open '<path>'`, once per entry, the path as the entry
gives it. Unattended, the human answers in the console, which shows every
board as a thumbnail, so nothing opens on this machine's screen.

blocks.title: Present the in-pane gate form
blocks.label: Present pane form
blocks.summary: The paneAction: form branch (older sites say the presentation: "form" branch).
blocks.text:
### Present the in-pane gate form

The `paneAction: form` branch (older sites say the
`presentation: "form"` branch). Show `formContext`, when present, in the
pane before the first chunk, then ask `formChunks` in order, one
AskUserQuestion call per chunk, rendering each chunk as given; answer once,
after the last. Dismissed: another surface answered, and the doorbell is
your next input. Cancelled: the gate stays open; never re-present it
yourself.

### Map the gate answer to exact option values

`answers` is one object keyed by question id, values per Answers are option
values (below); a question with no options takes the human's text, and
words at a held gate map the same way. On a `writeIn` question, "Other"
text with nothing ticked is `{"writeIn": "<text>"}`, never the nearest
option; beside ticks on a multi it is `{"value": [<ticks>], "note":
"<text>"}`. A refused value is remapped once, counted as in Fix what the
gate_ask refusal names, then left open for another surface.

blocks.title: gate_reconcile status?
blocks.label: Reconcile status
blocks.summary: It re-reads the gate (up to 2 seconds), records the answer under a run and clears waiting-gate; never a timed rt gate wait or a hand record.
blocks.text:
### gate_reconcile status?

It re-reads the gate (up to 2 seconds), records the answer under a run and
clears `waiting-gate`; never a timed `rt gate wait` or a hand record. Late
means `alreadyReconciled`, a `skipped` naming a stale gate, or, with no run,
a gate this pane already acted on. Otherwise `answered` is the decision, and
words in hand lose to it. `open` with words: map them and let
`gate_answer`'s CAS decide; with none, end the turn again (the wait and
marker stand). A daemon-unreachable refusal takes the daemon-down branch,
quoting it.

### A write-in to act on (actOnWriteIn)?

any other `next` (Hold, Go back, Abandon) was picked on purpose, and the
site takes it with the write-in as its note. With no tool result, apply the
rule yourself.

the whole answer set, then open a NEW gate at the same site so the human
sees the result first. One too unclear to act on goes straight to that new
gate, which asks about it.

blocks.summary: A site that says "run gate-protocol's Runs integration with kind <k> and these questions" enters at the trigger and walks every branch.
blocks.text:
### Runs integration

A site that says "run gate-protocol's Runs integration with kind `<k>` and
these questions" enters at the trigger and walks every branch. Under a run
every gate tool call passes `runDb` and the site's `stage`: the tools
bracket the gate, arm `waiting-gate` on a wait, record the answers map
(`decidedBy` the CAS winner) and clear the marker. Without them the stop
hook bounces the turn. With no run, omit both; nothing here calls a `run_*`
tool.

- **Every site is on the tools.** No host brackets a gate with
  `run_field_set {key: gate}` or records its answer with a `run_decision`
  gate@1 line: the tools record the answers map (a write-in as `{"writeIn": "<their
  words>"}` in that question's slot), and `Selection:` lines only name its
  keys. The board's wrappers run under no run, so they pass neither.
- **Review shapes.** `gate_answer` and `gate_reconcile` record nothing on a
  review gate (`respond-plan`, `respond-post`, `review-post`, scope `post`)
  unless passed `record: true`; the site records with `gate_record`.

blocks.label: Off script gate
blocks.summary: A host STOP opens it through the graph: scope off-script:<site>:<n> (n from 1 within the site's attempt), context quoting the refusal or the line asking for…
blocks.text:
### Off-script gate

A host STOP opens it through the graph: scope `off-script:<site>:<n>` (`n`
from 1 within the site's attempt), `context` quoting the refusal or the
line asking for the move.

| Question | Options |
|---|---|
| `action` | **Take the proposed move** (its value spells the whole move) / **Hand back** |
| `next` | **Proceed** (Recommended) / **Iterate here** / **Hold** |

Take: make exactly that move once, then continue from the node it led to.
Hand back: under a run, `run_stage {action: fail}` with the why as reason;
with no run, end the verb quoting it.

Hand back: under a run, `run_stage {action: fail}` with the why as reason;
with no run, end the verb quoting it.

blocks.text:
### Answers are option values

An answer to a question with options is one of its option VALUES verbatim
(an array on a multi), never an index, label or paraphrase. Nuance rides
`{"value": ..., "note": "..."}`; an edited replacement for offered text
rides `text`, which the in-pane form never sends. The verb's act step
decides what either changes. A `writeIn: true` question may instead take
`{"writeIn": "<their words>"}` alone.

blocks.text: ## Wrap-up form contract

segments.text: ## Wrap-up form contract

blocks.title: Wrap-up
blocks.label: Wrap up form
blocks.summary: The reply is one optional sentence of context, then a form, then stop.
blocks.text:
### Wrap-up

The reply is one optional sentence of context, then a form, then stop. Wait
for the answers before doing more work.

The form is this runtime's structured-question tool (`AskUserQuestion` in
Claude Code). One question per open item, in three buckets; omit an empty
bucket:

| Bucket | The question is | Options |
|---|---|---|
| Important details | a confirmation or pick among facts that still matter | concrete values |
| Decisions | a choice only the user can make | the real alternatives, recommended first and labelled `(Recommended)` |
| Next steps | whether or in what order to do remaining work | do now / later / skip |

Single or multiple choice as the item needs. If the tool caps how many
questions fit in one call, fill the first call and wait; the rest go in the
next call after the answers return, never into the context sentence.

| Thought | Reality |
|---|---|
| "A summary with the options listed is just as clear" | A list is text the user has to type back. The form is the answer channel. |
| "They asked me to be quick, so a compact list" | The form is the quick version: one tap per item. |
| "The options are obvious, prose is faster" | Obvious to you. The form records which one they picked. |
| "Next steps can go in prose after the form" | Next steps are questions: do now / later / skip. |
| "I can hand them a default to save them answering" | Recommended options already do that in the form; a typed reply still costs more than a tap and leaves no record of the pick. |
| "The context sentence, then a line introducing the form" | Two sentences. The form needs no introduction; the sentence is the whole preamble. |
